Measles cases in Europe rose sharply last year, WHO says

GENEVA (Reuters) - Measles cases in Europe rose 30 percent in 2023 compared with the previous year, the World Health Organization said in a statement released on Tuesday.

Dr. Hans Kluge, the WHO regional director for Europe, said vaccination coverage had fallen during the COVID-19 pandemic and that gaps in immunity had allowed the virus to spread. "We must close the immunity gaps," Kluge told reporters at a briefing in Copenhagen.

The agency said 42,000 cases were reported across 41 countries. Health ministries in Romania and Kazakhstan reported the largest outbreaks, according to the published data. UNICEF said routine immunisation programmes were being expanded with support from the European Commission.

Officials said the figures were based on reports submitted by national health authorities and could be revised as more data became available.
